headlines.title: 4 arrested in shooting of 49ers player Keion White at San Francisco nightclub
headlines.description: Four suspects have been arrested in connection with the February shooting of San Francisco 49ers player Keion White at a Mission District nightclub, San Francisco officials announced Wednesday. The arrests were made in various cities across California and Georgia following a monthslong investigation that included more than 50 search warrants and assistance from over 250 law enforcement personnel, officials said. White, a defensive lineman for the 49ers, was shot in the early morning hours of Feb. 9 at a nightclub located on the 1700 block of Mission Street, according to police. “It started when multiple suspects, some brandishing firearms, confronted the 49ers player, which then led to a physical altercation between the group and the victim, who was shot in the leg,” San Francisco police Chief Derrick Lew said. White has since recovered following surgery and has been playing for the 49ers this season. Keion White May 2 Ricky Pearsall Sep 19, 2025 Following several months of investigation, officers last week served four no-bail arrest warrants. Atlanta police arrested 38-year-old Marquis Davis at his home last Wednesday. Officers found an illegal firearm, 820 grams of MDMA, 1,026 grams of methamphetamine, 979 grams of cocaine and 3,842 grams of fentanyl, police said. That same morning, San Francisco police and San Joaquin County sheriff’s deputies arrested 36-year-old Antoine Washington in Stockton. Officers recovered a loaded firearm, more than 120 oxycodone pills and roughly $7,000, according to police. In Southern California on the same day, San Francisco police and Irvine police took 35-year-old Curtis Green into custody without incident. The fourth suspect, 36-year-old Gregory Walker of Mountain House, was arrested last Friday in Los Angeles for his alleged involvement in the shooting, police said. Walker has since been charged with assault with a firearm with allegations that he personally discharged that firearm at White, San Francisco District Attorney Brooke Jenkins said. Walker also was charged with possession of a firearm by a felon, possession of a concealed firearm by a felon and possession of a loaded firearm by a felon. Jenkins said the district attorney’s office filed a motion to keep Walker in custody because they believe he poses a public safety risk. His arraignment is scheduled to take place Wednesday afternoon. Green faces multiple misdemeanors, including brandishing a firearm and carrying a concealed weapon, Jenkins said. “We will not tolerate any type of violence in our city, but certainly not gun violence,” Jenkins said. “We had a great, amazing Super Bowl weekend that ended with this incident. I am just so thankful to the San Francisco police that we are being able to hold those accountable who sadly chose violence on that night.” San Francisco police are working with the district attorney’s office and prosecutors in other jurisdictions to arrange for Davis and Washington to be transferred to the city to face charges, Lew said. The February shooting marked the second time in two years that a 49ers player was shot in the city. Wide receiver Ricky Pearsall was shot and injured during an alleged attempted robbery in Union Square in August 2024. He made a full recovery. NBC News contributed to this report.

headlines.title: DOJ threatens legal action against California over alleged noncitizen voters
headlines.description: The Justice Department is threatening legal action against California unless state and local officials review a list of potential noncitizens on their voter rolls. Acting Deputy Attorney General R. Trent McCotter sent letters to California Secretary of State Shirley Weber and Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder Dean Logan on Tuesday demanding that they review a list of possible noncitizens the federal government identified by noon on Thursday. “Allowing noncitizens to vote cancels citizen votes,” McCotter wrote in letter, which was obtained by NBC News. McCotter wrote that the DOJ provided a password-protected thumb drive with a list of individuals the federal government “believes are likely noncitizens who were sent a vote-by-mail ballot” for the 2026 election. He asked that county election officials “segregate — not cancel — those individuals’ vote-by-mail ballots” until their citizenship status was determined. “This should not be controversial, as the criminal statute is clear: only American citizens may vote in federal elections,” a Justice Department spokesperson said in a statement. “It is a federal crime for noncitizens to vote in U.S. elections, and the DOJ is asking California to ensure that is not occurring.” Reuters first reported on the letters. Justin Levitt, an NBC News contributor who was a Justice Department official during the Obama administration, said the federal government has no authority supporting its demands. “They can send the letter,” he said. “California doesn’t have to do anything about it.” Federal law prohibits systemic list maintenance within 90 days of a federal election. At this point, less than three weeks out from Election Day, the only changes to the voter rolls can come from individualized information, like notification from the Social Security Administration that someone has died. A DOJ spokesperson said the department is asking California to sequester ballots, not change their voter list. In a statement Wednesday, Logan said his office had not accessed the thumb drive the DOJ provided “because doing so would conflict with established data privacy and information security protocols.” He added that, “We do not consider the device a secure medium.” “Maintaining accurate voter registration records is a fundamental responsibility of our office,” Logan said in the statement. “Federal and state laws are clear on how voter eligibility is established — and any action to remove a voter from eligibility must be based on verifiable information, not assertions of unconfirmed data matching.” Weber did not respond to requests for comment. Trump Administration 15 hours ago Immigration 22 hours ago All registered voters in California receive mail-in ballots, which started going out on Oct. 5. The legal threats came amid a broader campaign by the Trump administration to zero in on what voting experts say is a relatively rare phenomenon of voting by noncitizens. Trump has long made unfounded claims that voting is marred by widespread fraud. Election officials in a several states — including Georgia, Connecticut, Nevada, and Washington state — say they have received federal subpoenas in recent months for election records. Some officials said they fear these actions were designed to set up possible legal challenges after the midterm elections. “What we have seen is some groundwork laid out for post-election challenges,” said Stuart Holmes, the director of elections in Washington state. “Whether that’s the seizure of voting equipment, ballots themselves, tabulation equipment … we’re preparing for any and all eventualities in that case.” Nevada Secretary of State Cisco Aguilar, a Democrat, said officials in his state are also preparing for potential challenges to this November’s results. He added that he viewed the administration’s moves as “an effort to dissuade people from participating in the elections.” “You have a president who’s trying to choose the voter base rather than the voters choosing the elected, and that’s not how our democracy works,” he said in an interview. “It’s the people control our elections, and when you try to take that control out, you do it through intimidation, you do it through threats, and you do it by trying to dissuade people from participating.” Levitt agreed with the election officials’ conclusions. “Are they laying the groundwork to say that voting was fraudulent? Of course they are. 100% they are,” he said, referring to the Trump administration. “Is the boy who cried wolf going to cry wolf? Yes, that’s what the boy who cried wolf does.” Since Trump took office, his administration has brought over 100 cases involving allegations of voting by non-citizens. More than 154 million people voted in the 2024 election, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. During the second Trump administration, the DOJ has sought voter registration data from every state in the country. It has filed lawsuits against 30 states and Washington, D.C., for refusing.
headlines.source: Ryan J. Reilly and Jane C. Timm | NBC News

headlines.title: Caltrans works to raise flood-prone Highway 37 ahead of El Niño storms
headlines.description: As California prepares for a potentially powerful El Niño, Caltrans is racing to raise a flood-prone North Bay highway before the winter storms arrive. Highway 37 near Mare Island has flooded repeatedly over the years. On Wednesday, crews were working to raise parts of the highway near the island by about three feet. Additional work will require a 55-hour closure of the highway in both directions between Mare Island and Sears Point staring next Friday night. The highway is scheduled to reopen by 5 a.m. on Monday, Oct. 26. “We’re going to be grading the top level of asphalt down that’s started to crack so we get to the sub-surface,” Bart Ney with Caltrans said. “Then we’re going to be adding concrete, a fill in to get it up, and then paving back over the top of it.” Caltrans said the work is designed to help reduce flooding risks on the vital commuter route.

headlines.title: Naked woman statue in San Francisco taken down
headlines.description: A landmark statue of a naked woman along San Francisco’s Embarcadero is coming down. The 45-foot illuminated statue was positioned in front of the Ferry Building for the past 18 months, but crews started taking it down Tuesday. The statue was originally created for the 2015 Burning Man festival and was later moved to the city as part of an outdoor art initiative called the Big Art Loop. It originally was supposed to only stay for six months. The piece was created by Bay Area artist Marco Cochrane and now is available for sale or lease on his website.

headlines.title: Netflix to cut about 6% of worldwide staff
headlines.description: Netflix is eliminating about 6% of its employee roster, or roughly 1,000 jobs, in a round of layoffs announced internally Wednesday, according to a source with knowledge of the matter. “Our mission — to entertain the world — is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources,” Netflix co-chief executives Greg Peters and Ted Sarandos said in an email to staff members Wednesday. The news was first reported by The Wall Street Journal. The source with knowledge of the matter confirmed the newspaper’s reporting was accurate. Netflix remains one of the titans of streaming, but it has struggled to boost user engagement on the platform. The service’s users watched more than 97 billion hours of content in the first half of 2026, an increase of 2% year-over-year, according to the company’s most recent quarterly earnings report. “Overall, we’re not growing as fast as I want us to, and we’re working on making that move faster,” Sarandos said at Bloomberg’s annual media conference late last month. Netflix is expected to report its third-quarter financial results next Tuesday. The majority of the job cuts will be concentrated in Netflix’s product, technology, legal and human-resources teams. Peters and Sarandos said the streaming firm will “continue to invest aggressively in high impact areas” while also “making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees and investors.” In recent months, Netflix has looked for ways to boost subscriber engagement, including adding live sports programming and video podcasts licensed from third-party companies such as Bill Simmons’ The Ringer. Netflix’s layoffs come as other major Hollywood studios look to reduce costs and streamline operations. The Walt Disney Co. has cut hundreds of jobs this year under new Chief Executive Josh D’Amaro, according to a source familiar with the matter. David Ellison’s Skydance is widely expected to shrink its work force across Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery.

headlines.title: Motorcyclist killed in crash on I-780 in Vallejo
headlines.description: A motorcyclist died after a crash on Interstate Highway 780 in Vallejo on Wednesday morning, according to the California Highway Patrol. Just before 7:30 a.m., a 64-year-old man from Santa Rosa riding a Honda Fury motorcycle struck the back of a Ford F-150 while driving on eastbound I-780 near Glen Cove Road. The motorcyclist was taken to Kaiser Permanente Vallejo Medical Center, where he was pronounced dead.

headlines.title: Bay Area faces fire weather concerns as temperatures rise
headlines.description: Warmer temperatures and dry conditions are expected across the Bay Area through Friday, raising fire weather concerns in higher elevations, particularly in the North Bay interior mountains, according to the National Weather Service. Moderate offshore winds are expected, with the strongest winds projected for Thursday, increasing the risk of fires spreading quickly if a fire starts. Temperatures will continue to rise through the end of the workweek, with the warmest conditions expected Friday. Inland areas could reach the mid-80s to mid-90s, while parts of the Peninsula and Santa Cruz Mountains could see highs in the upper 80s to mid-90s. The forecast led PG&E to notify more than 11,000 customers in the North and East Bay that they may have their power shut off between Wednesday evening and Saturday to avoid sparking wildfires. The power outages, which PG&E calls Public Safety Power Shutoffs, are expected to affect about 70,000 customers in 29 counties across the utility’s service range. In the Bay Area, that includes an estimated 4,705 in Alameda County, 1,605 in Contra Costa County, 3,027 in Napa County, 30 in Solano County, and 1,783 in Sonoma County. Meanwhile, a Coastal Flood Advisory remains in effect through 4 p.m. Wednesday for bayshore locations along San Pablo Bay. High tides could flood low-lying areas, cause isolated road closures and increase coastal erosion. PG&E 24 hours ago Microclimate Forecast 23 hours ago Forecast: Warmer ahead

headlines.title: Power outage affects hundreds in downtown Novato
headlines.description: A power outage is affecting downtown Novato on Wednesday morning, according to PG&E and local police. The outage was reported at 8:44 a.m. and is affecting 912 customers. PG&E on its outage map website said power is not expected to be restored until 6:45 p.m. Novato police said traffic signals are out in the area affected by the outage, and drivers should treat those intersections like ones with four-way stop signs. No information about what caused the outage was immediately available. The outage was unrelated to PG&E’s Public Safety Power Shutoffs planned for more than 11,000 customers in the North and East Bay starting Wednesday evening and going through Saturday to avoid sparking wildfires during dry and windy weather.

headlines.title: South Bay woman dies after car plunges off parking garage in Hawaii
headlines.description: A South Bay woman died last Friday after her car plunged five stories off a parking garage in Hawaii. The deadly plunge happened at a condominium complex in Honolulu. Investigators said the car, driven by an 84-year-old woman from San Jose, crashed through a retaining wall and fell about five stories before landing on the sidewalk below. Investigators were trying to figure out what led up to the crash. No one else was hurt.

headlines.title: Santa Rosa police arrest woman for alleged attempted child abduction
headlines.description: Officers in Santa Rosa arrested a woman on suspicion of attempted child abduction earlier this week, police said. On Monday just after 8 a.m., officers received a report regarding a mother walking with her young children when she was confronted by another woman. The mother was in the 700 block of Seventh Street with her toddler and a 10-month-old baby when an unknown woman aggressively approached them and prevented them from leaving the area, the Santa Rosa Police Department said in a statement Tuesday. The suspect allegedly demanded access to the baby, who was strapped into a stroller. The woman said she was going to take the child and reached into the stroller, grabbing at the baby. She then allegedly pulled on the stroller and continued to make statements about taking the baby. The mother called out for help, and a passing motorist stopped to help. The suspect fled the area before officers arrived. Neither child suffered physical injury. On Tuesday, detectives found a photo of a person of interest that was captured by an area security camera. At about 1:10 p.m., an officer saw a woman matching the photograph in the area of Second and D streets. The woman was arrested on suspicion of attempted kidnapping, child endangerment, and violating her pretrial release. Police believe the same suspect approached a woman walking her dog on Slater Street, where the suspect allegedly challenged the woman unprovoked and followed her.

headlines.title: SJ landlord killed by police after opening fire during tenant dispute on Locke Drive
headlines.description: A landlord-tenant dispute in South San Jose turned deadly Sunday night when a 69-year-old man was shot and killed by police following an exchange of gunfire. The series of events unfolded Sunday night, starting with an argument between the suspect and his tenant over rent and household guests. According to San Jose Police Chief Paul Joseph, “Initial reports of the confrontation describe the landlord as having a handgun in his pants pocket as he repeatedly pushed a guest of a tenant.” The suspect was identified as 69-year-old Ted Lieu. Police were initially unable to determine if a crime had occurred, and the victims did not want to pursue charges, so officers left the scene. However, about an hour later, the same tenant called 911 again. Chief Joseph said the caller “reported that the landlord was standing in the hallway of the house holding a shotgun threatening her and preventing her and another roommate from leaving the residence.” When police arrived, they found that Lieu had fled the location. Officers safely removed the victims from the home and began searching the area, locating Lieu hiding in a shed just a few houses down. Investigators say he ultimately opened fire. “During the encounter with the armed suspect it appears based on early stages of evidence processing that he discharged at least one round in the direction of officers,” Chief Joseph said. Three officers returned fire, and Lieu was pronounced dead at the scene. During the investigation, a firearm was recovered, alongside an assault rifle found at the suspect’s residence and a third firearm discovered in a garbage can. Investigators noted that Lieu had a history of conflict with neighbors and tenants involving firearms, as well as a prior history with law enforcement. The shock of the incident is still settling in for residents along Locke Drive. “It breaks our heart and right now our whole street is very concerned, very sad about the situation, what’s happening; I never would have pictured something like this happening in our neighborhood,” said neighbor Lilia Gaspar. Gaspar added, “I never would have pictured him doing something like this, I know he had a drinking problem, but I’ve known him for many years and I don’t know what could have gone through his mind.” Fortunately, none of the officers were injured. Chief Joseph stated that all three involved officers had several years of experience on the police force. The Santa Clara County District Attorney’s Office is investigating the shooting.

headlines.title: PG&E warns Bay Area customers of possible shutoffs amid high winds, dry conditions
headlines.description: Thousands of Pacific Gas and Electric customers across the Bay Area could lose power as early as Wednesday, including thousands in Alameda and Contra Costa counties. PG&E is concerned power lines could move or snap in the wind and spark a wildfire. The utility has posted a map online showing areas where customers have been notified about a potential Public Safety Power Shutoff. The shutoffs are expected to begin around 5:30 p.m. Wednesday and could last until Saturday afternoon. PG&E has warned 70,000 customers across 29 California counties that they are at risk of losing power, including more than 1,600 customers in Contra Costa County and more than 4,700 in Alameda County. Andrew McKoskey, who lives on Finley Road, is among the customers who received a text from PG&E warning that the power could be off for the next few days. For McKoskey, his pregnant wife and their 2-year-old son, the timing could be difficult. “Kinda lame because my wife’s about to go into labor,” McKoskey said. “Tomorrow’s her due date.” McKoskey said he hopes neighbors can help run the family’s generator while they are at the hospital so they don’t lose their food. “The reason we call these PSPS events is strictly for safety,” a PG&E spokesperson said. PG&E says early alerts give customers time to prepare, with possible outages lasting through Saturday afternoon. “We encourage you to be prepared now, start charging appliances and electronics, things like your electric vehicles or your phones,” said Tamar Sarkissian, a PG&E spokesperson. PG&E isn’t alone in taking precautions. Contra Costa fire officials are also monitoring the winds and plan to increase staffing if needed. “Anytime you have an offshore wind… the ability for fuel to lead to catastrophic fire danger,” said David Watson, assistant chief with the Contra Costa County Fire Protection District. PG&E says the areas affected could change depending on the weather. The utility is encouraging customers to check their address and sign up for alerts. Customers can look up their address online to find out if their location is being monitored for a potential safety shutoff at pge.com/pspsupdates. For more information on the possible PSPS, visit PG&E’s power shutoff forecast page.
